narrativeProgression.description: The narrator recounts the origins of BlueDot and its founder's mission to improve disease tracking.
The narrator describes BlueDot's successful prediction of the Zika outbreak in 2016 and its early warning about the COVID-19 outbreak in December 2019.
He shifts the focus to the problem of trust in information from public health officials.
He reflects on the evolving perception of AI, moving from a buzzword to a tangible reality.
He engages the viewers, inviting them to share their thoughts on the potential of AI.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: It is March 2020 and the whole world is talking about this new coronavirus.
Now, the World Health Organization, they first learned about it from the outbreak in China,
in January.
But one source warned about it already in December.
And this one source was not an epidemiologist or a physician.
This December warning of a new virus came from an AI named BlueDot.
So that's today's topic, Smart Machines.
So after the SARS epidemic, 17 years ago, an infectious disease specialist in Toronto,
Cameron Con, started to work on his mission to find a better way to track diseases.
In 2014, he founded a company called BlueDot.
And today, it looks like their disease surveillance analytics program is working.
So this machine uses natural language processing and machine learning to read news reports
in 65 languages.
And then it adds on reports of animal disease outbreaks.
Plus, it also reads airline data to predict where infected patients might end up.
And one of the successful predictions of BlueDot was the location of the seek outbreak
in South Florida in 2016.
And now it seems like this Smart Machine did it again by sounding the alarm bell here
on December 31, 2019.
And also predicting that this virus would jump from Wuhan to Bangkok, Seoul, Taipei, Tokyo,
and others.
I mean, Colorado today.
And here in the US, used like in many countries, truth from public health officials seems
to be a problem.
So maybe an AI-driven epidemiologist is what we need, not only for faster information,
but also for trustworthy and accurate information.
Up until now, we have been talking about artificial intelligence, but honestly, it's been
more of a bus word.
Most people would probably have a hard time to give a concrete example of what it really
is.
It would mention Syria or Alexa, and that's about it.
I believe this will change and 2020 will mark the start of the AI revolution.
This is the year where we will hear about autonomous cars and ships and things like that,
not only as experiments anymore, but out in the open, up and running.
And maybe we shouldn't refer to it as artificial intelligence.
Maybe it's easier to understand what's going on if we talk about machine learning.
Things that not only do what the programmer tell them to do, but actually learn by themselves
and thereby they get better over time.
So much faster, much more accurate.
It's quite easy to see that the change ahead of us is much more turbulent than the change
we have been through.
So what do you think about this?
What's your thoughts on machines smarter than human beings?
See any new problems or opportunities?
Please share them in the comments section and interact down below.
And if you want more, make sure to subscribe.
And wash your hands and don't pick your nose.
Even simple biological intelligence should know that by now.
See you in the future.

youtube_description:
Artificial Intelligence is, up until today, mostly a story about buzzwords and the narrative of dangerous technologies that will take our jobs or even pose an existential threat to humanity. 
Maybe the Corona (COVID-19) pandemic will mark the start of the real AI revolution. 
A machine can work around the clock, tirelessly, and with incredible speed, making the process vastly more scalable, timely, and efficient. 
But, a machine can also present information and conclusions without bias and political objectives, so maybe the relevant question for the 21st-century isn't whether we can trust in AI but for how long we can do the opposite.
Who knows, maybe a machine will show us the way out of this crisis?

How AI May Prevent The Next Coronavirus Outbreak
https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonchandler/2020/03/05/how-ai-will-prevent-the-next-coronavirus-pandemic/
